author: kevaundray
content:
Ah I see, I need to think through a bit. 

Mostly thinking about the invariant that: if we have two conflicting checkpoints being finalised, then their 2/3 quorums are only guaranteed to share 1/3 stake, if both of their sets mostly overlap

If validators are exited immediately, I'm not sure that this invariant holds

author: jtraglia
content: Maybe we shouldn't immediately exit validators. As long at least ~70% of validators have registered PQ keys, the network should be functional. Seeing low participation would look bad, but it shouldn't really matter. Participation would go back to normal (99%+) after a few weeks/months. There would be an even greater incentive to register PQ keys because those that don't are going to lose quite a bit of stake due to penalties.

author: terencechain
content: haven't looked at the above, general comment is i think we need to separate withdrawal delay from validator set churn here. keeping funds locked doesn’t preserve quorum overlap if we immediately remove that stake from the active set, maybe we could schedule non PQ validators through normal exit churn, ideally starting before the fork
